brief: Deutsche Bank's Binky Chadha downgraded Tech to neutral three weeks ago, just before the sector underperformed the rest of the S&P 500 by more than 16 percentage points, pushing its relative performance to the bottom of a decade-long trend channel. Fifteen trading days later he is flipping back to overweight. Deutsche Bank counts five similar V-shaped Tech recoveries over the past 2.5 years, each averaging a 38% gain, and argues this rotation, while shallower, fits that pattern. Tech positioning has collapsed from elevated levels to the 40th percentile, which the note says implies roughly 10% earnings growth, versus 47% actually delivered in Q3 and consensus of 36% by the end of next year, meaning positioning has fallen faster than fundamentals. Tech revenue growth estimates have also been revised up over the past month. The note adds that earnings strength is broad, not just AI-driven: the median S&P 500 company is growing earnings 14.4%, near two-decade highs outside recession rebounds, and ex-Tech and Energy, growth is still 12%.
